decisions.issues: Minor only. Nagoji's collar ring sits at the front, not the side, and a short length of chain hangs from it down his chest. This is not above anyone's head, so it does not break the rule against vertical chains. A hanging lantern lights the hold warmly, so it is dim rather than near darkness. The pale slits overhead read as gaps in the deck seams, not open sky, which fits 1.3. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold ear stud, loose curly hair, torn ochre tunic, cream dhoti, bandaged wrists under the manacles, wrist chain, ankle cuffs with hobble chain, barefoot. His right hand lies flat on the planks. A ragged ochre flap covers his left forearm, so no brand shows. The image is tilted hard and upright boards split the pens. Pen chains run collar to collar and rise to the beams at a slant. There is no text, blood or anachronism. Hands and feet are sound. The dark, plain ceiling at top right easily holds both captions, and the dark foreground planks at bottom left are a second option. v01 to v04 were not offered as candidates in this round (they show open sky and storm through the hull).

Acceptable, with minor issues. The wide, distant view shows the broadside surge: water rushes down the aisle into the pens and the collar-to-collar pen chains snap sideways along the rows, never upward. There is no text, noose, blood or anachronism (glass lanterns are fine on a Portuguese ship). Minor points: the rendering is more photographic and cinematic than the inked neighbouring panels; the extras are bare-chested in loincloths rather than grey and brown rags; the tilt is modest and the 'almost weightless' moment is not really shown, since the men are bracing, which reads a little like galley rowers. The caption fits cleanly in the large dark ceiling area at top left (x 0.02 to 0.45, y 0.02 to 0.2).

Acceptable. This is a clean edit of the previously accepted v03 with the painted balloons removed and no artefacts left behind. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch3 row: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, torn ochre tunic with a ragged flap covering his left forearm, bandaged wrists, hinged collar. He shouts down the line while the men beside him copy the overhead grip. Deviations: he grips the beam with his hands apart instead of hooking both forearms over it with his wrists together, and his collar chain hangs down the front from the centre of the collar instead of drooping to one side from a side ring. The blue-lit grating at upper right reads as storm light through a hatch grating, not open sky. There is room for lettering over the low-detail beams at top left (x 0.0 to 0.3, y 0.0 to 0.18) and top right (x 0.6 to 0.98, y 0.0 to 0.2), clear of the raised hands.

Acceptable. This is a tight two-shot with Nagoji on the left and Keshavrao on the right, faces close and water streaming down them. Nagoji is on-model: curled moustache, light captivity stubble only, gold stud, ochre rags, bandaged wrists, collar. Keshavrao matches his sheet: short ragged hair, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, collar, no ear stud. The collar-to-collar chain droops between them. Nagoji's left forearm shows at the bottom from the outer side with a bandaged wrist and no brand, which is acceptable. Lettering room is limited to the dark top band (x 0.0 to 0.65, y 0.0 to 0.16) and the dark left edge (x 0.0 to 0.18, y 0.16 to 0.45). The two long lines may need balloons that just touch the top of Nagoji's hair, but no face would be covered.

Acceptable. Keshavrao is alone and on-model: short ragged hair, faint moustache, softer young face, grey-brown torn tunic, hinged collar with a side ring, no ear stud. His eyes are wide in the gloom, and lightning glows through the seams overhead. Minor points: the lightning does not really light half his face, which is lit evenly and warmly; the render is darker and more photographic than 3.4; his eyes glance screen-right, although Nagoji is off-panel to the left (placed by 3.4 and by the collar chain leaving the frame at left). The large, plain, dark plank wall on the left (x 0.02 to 0.5, y 0.02 to 0.6) holds all three balloons easily. The tail for Nagoji's off-panel line points to the left edge.

Minor only. The over-the-shoulder framing works: Keshavrao is seen from behind (short hair, grey-brown tunic, collar) and Nagoji matches his sheet (thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, collar, bandaged fists, ankle cuffs with a hobble chain), with his fist round the drooping chain. His left arm is wrapped in a ragged ochre sleeve rather than the sleeveless tunic, which still keeps the brand hidden. The forearm-long chain between his wrists is not clearly shown. The plank bowing inward behind him is not distinct. Water sheets down the walls, which is heavier than the scripted spray but reads as seepage through the hull, not rain. There is no painted text or balloons. For lettering, use the low-detail wall at upper right (about x 0.68 to 0.98, y 0.03 to 0.40) and the upper centre (x 0.30 to 0.65, y 0.0 to 0.17), away from Nagoji's face.

Keshavrao matches his sheet: short ragged wet hair, faint moustache, softer young face, grey-brown tunic, iron collar. The ghost of a smile is there, and there is no text. There is a painted white margin with a thin black frame line about 20 px in on every edge. Trim about 22 px from each side before placing it, or the panel gets a double border (tail and face fractions above refer to the untrimmed image). The background planks are warm, bright and softly blurred, with a slight mosaic upscale texture. That is lighter than the dark, cold-lit hold in 4.1, but acceptable for a tight close-up. For lettering, use the plain wall at upper right (x 0.62 to 0.97, y 0.04 to 0.45).

This is the closed hold, wide, with lightning lines through the deck seams and chained men clinging to beams and each other, mouths open and eye-whites showing. There is no text and no painted boxes. Minor points: the light comes through plank seams rather than specifically round a hatch cover, and it reads as a dim blue flicker more than one harsh white freeze-frame. The third man from the left has a faint reddish flush on his forehead. It is diffuse, with no gash or drip, so it does not read as gore at print size. The second man (curly hair, moustache) has stubble and no ear stud, so he should not be mistaken for Nagoji. Put the caption in the dark ceiling planks along the top (x 0.30 to 0.95, y 0.0 to 0.12).

Nagoji is on the left and matches his sheet: moustache, gold ear stud, clean chin with light captivity stubble, collar, bandaged wrists, manacles with a short chain, no brand visible. Keshavrao is on the right and matches his: short hair, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, collar. They are waist-deep, with chains dragging in the surge and a bearded prisoner gasping behind them. The ring bolted in the beam at upper right is clear, with the chain running to it. Hands are sound and there is no text. Minor points: Keshavrao shouts with his chin up but is not tight at Nagoji's ear (the prisoner sits between them), and he looks up-left rather than toward the ring. The background prisoner wears a small gold ear stud, though his full beard keeps him distinct from Nagoji. The warm golden light is warmer than the cool blue of 4.1. For lettering, use the ceiling beams across the top (the PRISONER balloon about x 0.35 to 0.55, y 0.03 to 0.20; the KESHAVRAO balloon about x 0.56 to 0.82, y 0.02 to 0.20), keeping the ring at about x 0.90, y 0.10 clear.

Clean pick. v06 is v05 (the version already accepted) with the painted balloon removed, and the repainted ceiling, beams and barrels in the upper right show no leftover marks. Nagoji matches his sheet and the chapter 3 row: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with light stubble, gold ear stud, long loose curly hair, torn ochre tunic, cream dhoti, bandaged wrists, short-chained manacles, hinged collar with a side ring. The tunic flap covers his left forearm down to the bandage, so the brand stays hidden. He rounds on the prisoners with teeth bared while they cry out with raised fists and reaching hands. The waist-deep flooded hold, warm light, barrels and dripping seams match 5.2 and 5.4. There is no text, noose, blood or anachronism, and all hands are sound. Two minor points: a small grated opening at the top left shows rain outside, which reads as a hull scuttle rather than open sky; and the left-hand pen chain disappears behind Nagoji's hip. Neither needs a regeneration. Put the single NAGOJI balloon over the low-detail beams and barrels up and to the right of his head, at about x 0.62 to 0.82 and y 0.03 to 0.30. It covers no face and no hand.

Minor only. The musket floats half-submerged at the surface in the near foreground instead of lying on the floor under the water. Keshavrao's moustache is a little fuller than 'faint'. A short loose chain hangs from Nagoji's right manacle into the water. Otherwise clean. Nagoji is on the left looking up at the lit hatch, with thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, empty collar with side ring and his left forearm covered by a tunic flap and bandage. Keshavrao is on the right looking at him. Both stand about thigh-deep. The dark ceiling beams across the top (x 0.45 to 0.92, y 0.0 to 0.2) take balloons 0 and 1, and the open water at the bottom centre (x 0.35 to 0.8, y 0.8 to 0.97) takes balloon 2.

Acceptable, with continuity notes. The camera looks up the ladder from a low angle. Nagoji climbs with both manacled, bandaged hands on the rungs and the musket pinned under his near arm, and the hobble chain is visible between his ankle cuffs. He looks back down with moustache, clean chin and gold stud intact, and the brand arm is wrapped. Keshavrao is seen from behind at the foot of the ladder, collar and manacle on, in the water. Notes: (1) Nagoji's iron collar is not visible. His hunched shoulder and long hair hide his neck, so it reads as hidden rather than removed, but it is a soft continuity gap against 6.2. (2) This ladder is round poles lashed with rope, where the ladders in 6.2 and 6.5 are plain wood. (3) A glass lantern and open-flame lamps burn in the hold, which 6.2 does not show. This is allowed in a Portuguese setting but is a small lighting change. Lettering: the Nagoji balloon goes in the dark ceiling at the upper left (x 0.18 to 0.45, y 0.02 to 0.15), with its tail to his mouth. The caption goes in the dark ceiling beams at the upper right (x 0.66 to 0.97, y 0.02 to 0.2).

Clean. This is Nagoji's point of view straight up the ladder. The guard is a black silhouette on the top rungs, backlit by lightning and rain in the open hatch. The upturned brim and crest of his morion read clearly. One hand grips the ladder rail and the other points the musket barrel down at the camera. There is no text, blood or anachronism. Minor: a dark twisted rope or post shows behind the lower rungs, and this ladder has no rope lashings, unlike 6.4. The GUARD balloon goes on the dark wood planks at the upper right (x 0.72 to 0.98, y 0.02 to 0.26), with a short tail to the silhouette's mouth under the helmet brim.

v11 (the only candidate) gets most of the correction right. It has a true side-on view across a flooded, lamp-lit timber hold and a flat-tread companion ladder rising to an open hatch with lightning and rain. Both men are on the ladder, and Nagoji's bare feet are on treads above thigh-deep black water with his ankle cuffs and hobble chain hanging. He drives a reversed musket butt-up with both bandaged hands. The guard wears a morion, cream shirt, buff jerkin and dark breeches, with nothing red. He is thrown off balance with both hands off the rail, and his musket spins away at the right. There is no text, blood or noose, and there is dark low-detail ceiling at top-left for the captions. It fails the Chapter 3 bible row and the page's own continuity in two ways. (1) Nagoji wears NO iron collar: his neck is bare at native zoom, while 7.2 and 7.4 on the same page show the empty hinged collar prominently, and the r3 correction asked for it by name. (2) His wrists show bandages with a chain dangling from them but no iron manacle cuffs. Lesser issues: (3) the butt drives into the guard's upper arm near the armpit, not his wrist; (4) no gold ear stud is visible; (5) at 1536 x 1024 (1.5:1), the frame does not match the page's 160 pt full-width strip (about 2.3:1).
decisions.correction: Keep v11 exactly as composed: the true side-on view from far back across the flooded, lamp-lit timber hold, the flat-tread companion ladder rising diagonally to the open hatch with lightning and rain falling through it, the guard near the top in steel morion, cream shirt, buff leather jerkin with a single cross-belt and dark breeches, thrown off balance with both hands off the rail and his musket spinning away into the dark at the right, and Nagoji halfway up the ladder with both bare feet on treads above the thigh-deep black water, driving his reversed musket butt-up with both bandaged hands, ankle cuffs and short hobble chain hanging. Fix Nagoji's irons, which were missing: he MUST wear the empty hinged iron collar, a dark iron band about two fingers wide closed round his neck with a small ring at the side, clearly visible against the skin below his jaw; and each bandaged wrist MUST carry a plain dark iron manacle cuff over the bandage, the two cuffs joined by a short slack chain about a forearm long that swings between his hands. Show his small gold ear stud. Let the heel of the butt strike the guard's lower forearm and wrist, just as that hand springs open and releases the musket, not his upper arm or armpit. Frame it as a wide band of about 2.3:1 (for example 1899 x 828) with both figures and the hatch in the middle band. Keep a plain, dark, low-detail area of ceiling timbers at top-left and a smaller one of dark water at lower-right, clear of both men, the musket and the hatch.

decisions.issues: v04 (the only candidate) is right about Nagoji and the beat. He is pressed flat to the flat-tread ladder, his cheek to the wood, eyes squeezed shut and face turned away from the fall. He has a thick curled moustache, a clean chin with light captivity stubble and a gold ear stud, and he wears the empty hinged collar with its side ring. His visible hand is bandaged, in an iron manacle with its chain, and his ankle cuffs and hobble chain are on a lower tread. The visible arm is his right, so the left forearm stays hidden. Lightning and rain fill the open hatch and black flood water glints below, which matches 7.1 and 7.4. There is no text, blood or noose. It fails on the falling guard. His sleeves are clearly crimson or maroon, and they still read red at thumbnail size. That breaks the r3 correction ('nothing red') and the page's continuity: the same guard wears a cream shirt and buff jerkin in 7.1 and 7.3. It also drifts toward the redcoat look that the standing rules forbid for Portuguese guards. Minor points: the left side of the hatch shaft shows a brick-like grid texture, and the frame is portrait (1024 x 1536) for a near-square slot of about 1.1:1.
decisions.correction: Keep v04 exactly: the steep close view beside the flat-tread companion ladder; Nagoji pressed flat to it with his cheek on the wood, eyes squeezed shut and face turned away from the fall; his thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, long curly hair, empty hinged iron collar with its side ring, torn ochre tunic and cream dhoti; his bandaged hand in its iron manacle with the chain running on; the ankle cuffs and hobble chain on a lower tread; the lightning and slanting rain in the open hatch above; and the black flood water glinting far below. Change only the falling guard, so that he is the same man seen in 7.1 and 7.3: a steel morion, cream linen shirt sleeves, a buff leather jerkin with a single cross-belt, dark breeches and boots. Render him as a near-black, motion-blurred silhouette backlit by the lightning, arms flung out and hands empty, grasping at nothing. There must be no red, crimson or maroon anywhere on him. Make the sides of the hatch shaft plain dark ship's timber, with no brick or stone texture. Compose for a near-square slot of about 1.1:1 (for example 1152 x 1024), so that the guard, Nagoji's face and his gripping hand all sit inside it.

decisions.issues: Clean and faithful to the r3 correction. The view is high, straight down the flat-tread companion ladder, with a brass lamp at left and lashed bales and barrels. The hold is flooded with no dry planks, and the lowest treads meet the water. The fallen guard floats face-down, half submerged, in a buff leather jerkin, cream shirt, dark breeches and boots. His face is hidden in the water and his morion floats beside him. The collared, manacled prisoners press back against the bales, waist-deep. There is no blood, text or noose, and the prisoners' hands are sound. The plain dark hull planking across the top-left (about x 0 to 0.42, y 0 to 0.12) is clear of every face for 'The ladder was clear.' Minor points only: the rendering is more photographic and less inked than 7.1 and 7.4 (the earlier 7.3 candidates shared this and were not faulted for it); the morion floats upright rather than upside down; and the body lies in open water by the barrels rather than pressed against the hull planks.

Clean. This is the r3-approved v03 composition with the painted balloon removed. Nagoji matches the sheet: thick curled moustache, a clean chin with light captivity stubble, a small gold ear stud, long curly hair, the empty hinged collar, a torn ochre tunic and a bandaged hand in an iron manacle, its chain running back to the hidden wrist. The visible arm is his right, so the left forearm stays hidden. He is half out of the timber hatch in driving rain, twisted round to shout down at the backs of the prisoners' heads. The flat-tread ladder matches 7.2 and 7.3, and the glass deck lantern is allowed in a Portuguese setting. There is no text, blood or noose. The rain-streaked sky and rigging above and right of his head (about x 0.57 to 0.88, y 0.02 to 0.24) is low-detail and clear of his face for the balloon. Two notes. (1) A cream frame border with a black keyline is painted round the edges (cream to about x 11 and from x 1524, to y 7 and from y 999, with the keyline just inside). Set visible_rect to about [16, 12, 1520, 993] to crop it out. (2) The blurred background deck figures, a sailor in a wide hat at left-centre and a crewman in a brimmed hat at right, have no readable faces and do not read as a guard confronting him.

v10 (the only candidate) gets Nagoji right: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold ear stud, iron collar with a side ring, torn ochre tunic, cream dhoti, bandaged wrists, bare feet with a hobble chain, and a rope coil at his feet as he clings to the starboard rail. The crew beat also works (knife in teeth, pumps, torn canvas, splintered mast), and there is clear sky at top left and top right for both captions. It fails on setting and text. (1) The carved stern castle at upper right is not part of this ship. It reads as a second galleon, seen transom-on from outside with stern windows and its own row of masts, riding the waves outboard of Nagoji's rail. The script has one ship alone in the storm, and 8.3, looking to starboard, shows only a wave and a spar. (2) That stern carries a gold name board of cursive pseudo-lettering at about x 0.88 to 0.91, y 0.33 to 0.36, which breaks the no-text rule. Smaller faults: (3) the right wrist wears two iron cuffs with a short chain dangling free, and the left wrist has a separate cuff. The wrists are not joined by the forearm-long chain, and the hands are too far apart for such a chain to reach. (4) Two background sailors near x 0.47 to 0.53, y 0.43 to 0.5 wear steel helmets, which read as soldiers rather than barefoot crew in caps or head cloths.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition: a wide, low angle along the heeled, rain-lashed deck; Nagoji in the right foreground braced against the starboard rail, gripping a line, a half-loose rope coil at his bare feet, hobble chain on his ankles, empty iron collar with its side ring; barefoot crew on the left at the pump handles and rigging, one with a knife in his teeth; the splintered mainmast and torn canvas in the centre; open storm sky with lightning at top left and top right for the captions. This is the ONLY ship in the panel, and no other vessel appears anywhere. Beyond Nagoji's rail there is only open black sea, breaking wave crests, spray and rain: no second hull, no stern gallery, no masts or rigging out on the water. This ship's own stern castle may appear only as a high dark deckhouse at the far end of the same deck the crew stand on. It is seen from inside the ship (its forward bulkhead and rails), never as a transom with stern windows seen from outside. It carries no name board, no carved lettering, no gilded scrollwork that looks like script, and no glyphs of any kind. Nagoji wears exactly one iron manacle on each wrist. Both hands grip the same line close together near the rail, no more than a forearm apart, and the short chain joining the two manacles hangs slack between them. The inner side of his left forearm faces away from the camera. Every sailor wears a knitted cap, a head cloth or nothing on his head: no metal helmets, no armour.

decisions.issues: Acceptable, with minor deviations. Keshavrao matches his sheet: short hacked hair, a young face, grey-brown tunic, white dhoti, an empty iron collar with a side ring, manacles, and no ear stud. He is half out of the hatch with his left hand clamped on the rim and his right hand at his side, and the inset of Nagoji's bandaged, manacled hand clawing the rope coil sits in the upper left. There is no painted text, balloon, blood or anachronism. Minor points: (1) His moustache is a little heavier than 'faint', but still thin and nothing like Nagoji's curled one. (2) His hair is spiky and wet, not slicked flat, and the hairline graze is barely visible (only a faint mark at the right temple). (3) The right hand reads more as hanging and bracing than as twitching for a missing sword. (4) The wrist chain runs from his right cuff to the waist and vanishes behind the tunic, so the slack between the wrists is vague. (5) In the inset both cuffs, joined by the chain, can read as sitting on one bandaged forearm. At inset size it passes as the chained pair of wrists, and the clawed hand shows 4 digits (thumb plus 3 fingers), which is plausible for the grip. (6) The deck is rain-slick rather than foam-awash, but the grey-white post-wave light fits 9.2. Lettering space: put the caption in the top band of the inset (about x 0.10-0.30, y 0.01-0.18 of the frame), above the fingers, over the blurred background. Put Keshavrao's balloon in the open rain sky at the upper right (about x 0.56-0.95, y 0.02-0.22), with its tail down-left to his mouth.
